source_title: Best Buy Co., Inc. Form 8-K exhibit - fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2015 results (Renew Blue turnaround)
company_context: Best Buy is a large US electronics retailer that entered fiscal 2013 in distress: margin erosion, declining comparable sales, and a reported GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $13 million in the quarter ended November 3, 2012, versus $173 million net earnings a year earlier, with showrooming and price pressure from online competitors. CEO Hubert Joly launched the multi-year 'Renew Blue' program (price-matching, vendor partnerships, store-within-store, online growth, cost reduction). By fiscal 2014-2015 the program delivered measurable cost reductions, returning comparable-sales growth, and earnings improvement.
business_type: Brick-and-mortar and omnichannel electronics retail, large store footprint, thin-margin and price-competitive
evidence_summary: Best Buy entered the turnaround in margin erosion: a GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $13 million ($0.04/share) for the quarter ended November 3, 2012 versus $173 million ($0.47/diluted share) a year earlier, with a 4.0% Domestic comparable-store-sales decline and pre-tax restructuring charges of about $203 million in Q4 FY13. Under the Renew Blue program the company cut about $350 million of costs in fiscal 2014 and reached cumulative cost reductions of about $965 million by Q3 fiscal 2015 (quarter ended November 1, 2014). Performance recovered: Q3 FY15 revenue of about $9.4 billion with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.32 versus $0.18 a year earlier and a 2.4% Domestic comparable-sales increase; Q4 FY15 revenue up 1.3% to about $14.2 billion with non-GAAP diluted EPS up 23% to $1.48 versus $1.20. The arc is a documented margin-erosion-to-turnaround case driven by cost discipline, price-matching, and omnichannel investment.

source_backed_metrics.q3_fy13_gaap_net_loss_continuing_ops_usd: $13 million ($0.04 per share), vs $173 million ($0.47 per diluted share) prior-year quarter

outcome_evidence: Transition from a Q3 FY13 net loss and negative comparable sales to positive Domestic comparable-sales growth (+2.4% Q3 FY15), large cumulative cost reductions (~$965 million by Q3 FY15), and double-digit non-GAAP EPS growth in Q4 FY15, evidencing a successful multi-year turnaround.
source_limitations: Figures are drawn from Best Buy 8-K earnings exhibits on the primary SEC EDGAR domain (sec.gov) as surfaced in verbatim search-result snippets; direct WebFetch of sec.gov returned HTTP 403 in this environment. Several recovery metrics are management non-GAAP figures (e.g., non-GAAP diluted EPS, cumulative cost reductions). Revenue figures rounded as reported.
